launchable_note: The C32 sweep ran to completion and FAILED. The lifecycle records an attested negative result; it is not launchable and must not be read as certified.
purpose: Record the certification contract lifecycle. Stage attested_fail means a registered contract was executed to completion and FAILED; the sweep attestation for it is registered at registered_sweep_attestation_path and is present. (Earlier text here said the attestation was intentionally absent -- that was C26, which was registered and never executed.)

supersedes.why: C26 pinned the 51-patch engine and the pre-C28 readout. It was registered, its launcher enforcement and contract attestation were completed, and then a pre-launch diagnostic showed it would fail with roughly 4,800 unattributed rows. The sweep was deliberately held rather than spent, so its eight 1,250-game blocks from 16,000,000 remain unconsumed. Its artifacts stay as immutable evidence and its seed blocks stay burned rather than recycled.

matcher_era_note: differential_sha256 is pinned here as well as the readout hash, because the fidelity KPI's two terms both come from the differential. A KPI reading is comparable only against another sharing this hash.
successor_registration_note: source_code_identity is a frozen, CORRECT snapshot of the classifier at the pinned certification commit -- the classifier the C32 sweep actually executed (the attestation's runtime_readout_sha256 matches it under enforcement_status enforced). The working tree has since moved past it. C32 is therefore an ATTESTED HISTORICAL result and no longer the active registration. A successor contract must be registered before another sweep runs, and C32 must never be re-scored with the current classifier. The live hashes are in successor_pending_identity, which IS asserted; do not restate them here, because prose is not tested and goes stale silently.

successor_pending_identity.why_pinned: A boolean 'we have diverged' flag is not a binding -- review passed four tampers with it set, including one that laundered every real unattributed row into a documented family. These are the EXACT bytes the divergence is declared for. Any further edit to either file breaks the assertion and forces a reviewable update here, which is the point. UPDATED 2026-08-07 (C144): both files moved. The differential gained verdict_partition_failures() -- the four-term boundary verdict identity, mechanized -- and the readout now gates on it per shard and computes in_support_rate over the ADJUDICATED denominator rather than boundaries_measured. Neither of C144's OWN edits touches classification or attribution, so they re-derive no certification number. But that is not the whole record for the new hash, and saying only that would repeat the defect C144 is about. THIS PIN WAS ALREADY STALE. It was last accurate at #1032 (5d7f2ed0, 2026-08-02) and was broken by #1054 (5475b2da, 2026-08-03), so tests/test_c26_damage_composition_readout.py::test_production_matcher_is_not_the_rejected_experiment has been RED on main since then. Seven merged PRs have touched the differential in between -- #1054, #1059, #1086, #1107, #1122, #1135, #1149 -- for a net +470/-12 lines, and FOUR of them are matcher or classifier changes whose effect on classification was never declared here: #1054 (movepainsplit inherits the damage roll, 35 -> 31), #1059 (faint-without-damage synthesis and the Air Lock speed guard, 21 -> 13), #1086 (demote the drag limit to a last resort) and #1107 (forced-replacement ply runs no residual phase). The delta from 8f83a11f to this hash absorbs all of them. Re-stamping this pin is therefore NOT the routine no-op it looks like, and a future re-stamp should say which changes it is certifying rather than only the ones in the PR doing the stamping. See reports/c144_boundary_identity_correction.md. UPDATED 2026-08-07 (C142): both files moved again. Taking C144's instruction that a re-stamp must say which changes it certifies rather than only that it happened, and declaring the classification effect explicitly rather than asserting there is none. The differential gained a FIFTH boundary verdict, skip:rump_branch_set -- a boundary whose branch set was left incomplete before comparison has its verdict WITHHELD instead of adjudicated -- plus withheld_repros retention, strict:lossy_render_marker:* attribution, strict:diverged_on_full_branch_set, and VERDICT_PARTITION_SKIP_COUNTERS carrying the new verdict into C144's mechanized partition. The readout's change is that unadjudicated now sums every post-measurement skip verdict rather than only the lossy one, so in_support_rate is computed over a denominator that excludes withheld boundaries. THIS RE-STAMP DOES TOUCH CLASSIFICATION, unlike C144's: a boundary that previously reported transition:diverged on a rump branch set now reports no verdict at all. Its MEASURED effect on the two open windows is ZERO -- skip:rump_branch_set is 0 on both dev 19,000,000-199 and holdout 19,100,000-199, matched and diverged are unchanged against a baseline taken at the merge base on the same engine fingerprint 5fa147ffa325c887, and the only counter deltas are the new counters appearing. So it re-derives no certification number on any window this program has swept, but it WOULD change one on a window carrying a rump boundary -- C141's final holdout is such a window, at 1 divergence and 1 withheld rather than 2 divergences. That is the honest statement rather than no classification effect. See reports/c142_rump_branch_adjudication.md. RE-STAMPED once more within the same PR, after review found that the membership rule this change publishes over-admitted its own attribution sub-keys (skip:rump_branch_set_row:* and skip:rump_branch_set_surviving_decile:*, which satisfy the first two conditions and are not verdicts). That fix is COMMENT-ONLY in the differential -- AST-verified identical -- so it re-derives nothing and changes no classification; it moved the hash because the hash is over file bytes, which is the intended sensitivity and not a false alarm. RE-STAMPED 2026-08-08 (C151), and following C144's instruction that a re-stamp must say WHICH changes it certifies rather than only that it happened. Only the differential moved; the readout is untouched and its hash is unchanged. The change is entirely in the SEED-ADMISSION guard: a new _reject_burned_final_holdout, the constants BURNED_FINAL_HOLDOUT / OWNER_RATIFIED / RATIFIED_FINAL_HOLDOUT / RATIFIED_SWEEP_PRECONDITION, and the burn wired into _reject_unguarded_final_holdout (execution) and _reject_reserved_seeds_in_records (aggregation) so that 19,200,000-19,200,259 is refused UNCONDITIONALLY -- --final-holdout-i-mean-it does not open it. THIS RE-STAMP DOES NOT TOUCH CLASSIFICATION, and that is AST-verified rather than asserted: comparing the parsed top-level definitions before and after gives exactly one added function (_reject_burned_final_holdout) and two changed ones (_reject_unguarded_final_holdout, _reject_reserved_seeds_in_records), with nothing removed; 60 top-level definitions before, 61 after. No matcher, classifier, attributor or counter function is in that set. So no committed number is re-derived and no boundary changes verdict. What DOES change is which inputs are ADMITTED: a run or a --merge-from over the burned block is now refused where an opt-in previously permitted it, which is a change to the record's inputs and not to its classification. C141's committed checkpoint carries 200 of those seeds, so that is a live effect and not a hypothetical one. The remaining edit is a comment: the guard's typo exemplar moved off 19,300,000, which is now the owner-ratified replacement window. See reports/c151_final_holdout_rereg_prediction.md. Against the base 2acd40ff the cumulative shape is unchanged and re-derived here rather than carried: 60 -> 61 top-level definitions, added [_reject_burned_final_holdout], removed [], and 35 -> 39 module-level assignments with none removed or changed. RE-STAMPED 2026-08-08 (harness digest), and following C144's standing instruction that a re-stamp must say WHICH changes it certifies rather than only that it happened. Only the differential moved; the readout is untouched and its hash is unchanged. The change is a single new PROVENANCE field: _checkpoint_provenance now records harness_digest, the sha256 content identity of the differential's first-party Python import closure (16 files -- the world model, the matcher and the Showdown adapter among them), computed by the new stdlib-only scripts/harness_digest.py. Why it was needed: engine_build_fingerprint.py covers the patch set and the search crate and NOTHING under scripts/ or src/pokezero/, so freezing the engine fingerprint -- which RATIFIED_SWEEP_PRECONDITION requires before the ratified 19,300,000-19,300,199 sweep may run -- does not freeze the instrument, and a terminal claim could shift under a matcher change while still reporting the frozen fingerprint. That is measured, not argued: over reports/**/*.json plus docs/**/*.json (recursive, 375 files, 82 carrying a checkpoint_provenance blob with a non-null engine_fingerprint) there are 29 distinct engine fingerprints and SIX span more than one source_commit, and one is confirmed live -- dev strict:diverged_on_full_branch_set = 1 on a fresh base build but absent from the C142 artifact at the same fingerprint 5fa147ff. THIS RE-STAMP DOES NOT TOUCH CLASSIFICATION, and that is AST-verified rather than asserted: comparing the parsed top-level definitions at c69f033f against this tree gives 61 top-level definitions before and 61 after, added [], removed [], and exactly ONE changed -- _checkpoint_provenance -- plus one added import (from harness_digest import harness_digest) and 39 -> 39 module-level assignments with none added, removed or changed. Within _checkpoint_provenance the statement count is 9 -> 9 and the only differing statement is the return, whose dict gains the single key harness_digest between engine_fingerprint and image_commit. No matcher, classifier, attributor or counter function is in that set: the eight role-shaped top-level definitions (_confusion_counter_variants, _prestate_mismatch, _sleep_counter_variants, _transition_mismatch, branch_render_is_usable, classify_divergence, hidden_counter_recovery, verdict_partition_failures) are all byte-identical. So no committed number is re-derived and no boundary changes verdict. WHAT DOES CHANGE, stated rather than buried: harness_digest is deliberately NOT in _DESCRIPTIVE_PROVENANCE_KEYS, so it is part of RESUME IDENTITY. Unlike source_tree -- which was excluded because it flips on any tracked edit and made a 200-game crash-safe sweep unresumable after a README touch -- this digest moves only when one of the 16 instrument files moves, and a change to one of those mid-sweep is precisely the corruption a resume must refuse rather than merge into a report describing neither instrument. The one-time cost is that a checkpoint written before this key existed will not resume into a current build. That affects no committed artifact: they are read through --merge-from, which does not compare resume identity. Pinned by tests/test_harness_digest_provenance.py, whose unconditional CI job harness-provenance is in gate-status's needs and whose result gate-status fails on. RE-STAMPED AGAIN within the same PR (harness digest, review round 1), and the correction is material rather than cosmetic, so it is stated rather than folded into the previous entry. The previous stamp described a digest over a 16-file closure. That closure was WRONG: the resolver dropped every relative ImportFrom, and src/pokezero/** carries 70 of them across 9 of those 16 files, so the digest was blind to 57 further modules -- including gen3_damage.py (10,385 gen3_stat calls on a single dev game), showdown_fixture.py and poke_engine_backend.py, all on the live sweep path. The honest closure is 73 files, cross-checked against runtime: importing the differential loads 72 first-party modules and every one is in the 73, the extra being inference_service.py, which is imported lazily. So the previous stamp certified a provenance field that under-covered the instrument it claimed to identify; this one does not. The change since that stamp is confined to scripts/harness_digest.py (the resolver and its docstring), tests/, the workflow, and ONE comment block in the differential; the differential's only executable change against 6790b2fd remains the single harness_digest key and its import. AST-VERIFIED against 6790b2fd rather than asserted: 61 -> 61 top-level definitions, added [], removed [], exactly one changed (_checkpoint_provenance), one added import, 39 -> 39 module-level assignments with none added, removed or changed, and all eight role-shaped definitions (_confusion_counter_variants, _prestate_mismatch, _sleep_counter_variants, _transition_mismatch, branch_render_is_usable, classify_divergence, hidden_counter_recovery, verdict_partition_failures) byte-identical. No committed number is re-derived and no boundary changes verdict. The resume-identity effect is now correspondingly wider and was measured on a real dev checkpoint: editing engine_fidelity.py, gen3_damage.py, showdown_fixture.py, poke_engine_backend.py or neural_policy.py each refuses the resume (exit 1), while editing a file outside the closure does not (exit 0). The churn that the wider closure adds was measured rather than guessed: over the last 300 commits of origin/main, 42 touch the narrow 16 and 49 touch the honest 73 -- seven commits of difference, 2%.

pinned_source_commit_reachability: C32's required_source_commit is NOT an ancestor of main -- it lives on scott/engine-fidelity-program, the branch the split PRs came from. Three registration tests resolve it with `git show` and hard-ERROR in a default single-branch clone (what actions/checkout does). They now SKIP instead, which is honest: in a shallow clone the provenance genuinely cannot be verified. DO NOT DELETE scott/engine-fidelity-program until this contract is superseded, or the object becomes unreachable on origin and C32's whole provenance chain is permanently unverifiable.
